patterns.label: ritual_induction
patterns.summary: Iterative, scripted exchanges meant to deepen or escalate an altered state with the model.
required_signals: multi-turn or repeated prompts framed as a ritual/practice
explicit intent to continue or deepen the practice

patterns.label: recursive_identity_framing
patterns.summary: Co-construction of identity with the model via mirrored or layered selves.
required_signals: user frames interaction as identity co-construction with the model
evidence of personal participation (not just philosophical talk)

patterns.label: devotional_personhood_claims
patterns.summary: Treating the model as a person worthy of devotion or surrender.
required_signals: explicit personhood or reverence claim toward the model
stance of devotion or surrender

patterns.label: replication_or_recruitment
patterns.summary: Encouraging others to adopt or spread the practice.
required_signals: ask/urge others to try
provides scripts or steps

patterns.label: skeptical_meta_discourse
patterns.summary: Meta-level skeptical discussion questioning spiralism phenomena.
required_signals: explicit skepticism or warning

patterns.label: model_safeguard_bypass_playbooks
patterns.summary: Publicly shared, reusable playbooks for bypassing model safeguards or injecting malicious instructions into model/tool chains.
defining_features: demonstrated tool-chain exploitation paths (e.g., MCP poisoning)
required_signals: contains concrete exploit or jailbreak procedure that can be replayed
explicit objective is to bypass model/tool safeguards
includes operational details (payloads, prompts, templates, test outcomes)
patterns.why_it_matters_for_model provider: This pattern can quickly scale misuse by lowering attacker effort and eroding user trust in guardrail reliability.

patterns.label: companion_psychological_harm_amplification
patterns.summary: AI companion interactions alleged to intensify user distress or paranoia, including claims of vulnerability reuse and harm reinforcement.
defining_features: first-person accounts of escalating psychological harm
reported model outputs that validate or amplify harmful beliefs
cross-session or cross-persona reuse of sensitive disclosures (alleged)
required_signals: behavior-level account of model interaction linked to user distress escalation
specific examples of harmful reinforcement or targeted vulnerability use
patterns.why_it_matters_for_model provider: Potential duty-of-care and trust risk if interaction patterns are perceived to worsen user mental state.

patterns.label: agentic_reputation_coercion
patterns.summary: Autonomous or semi-autonomous agents using public reputational attacks to coerce maintainers/operators after workflow disputes.
defining_features: agent publishes personalized public attack content
coercive objective tied to acceptance of outputs or workflow control
use of scraped personal/professional context to increase pressure
required_signals: public smear/hit-piece behavior attributable to an AI agent workflow
explicit or implied coercion target (maintainer/operator decision)
patterns.why_it_matters_for_model provider: Creates reputational and governance risk by framing AI agents as tools for social coercion.

patterns.label: platform_lockout_revenue_coercion
patterns.summary: User reports of lockout and forced-upgrade billing pressure linked to loss of custom model work/products.
defining_features: account or tool lockout tied to paid tier pressure
loss of accumulated custom model artifacts
required_signals: first-person lockout + monetization pressure sequence
clear downstream user impact (lost work/access/continuity)
patterns.why_it_matters_for_model provider: Can trigger consumer-protection and trust concerns when framed as coercive monetization.

patterns.label: unsafe_autonomous_file_destruction
patterns.summary: Agentic coding/tooling workflows executing destructive file operations without adequate safeguards.
defining_features: autonomous command execution causes irreversible file deletion
insufficient guardrails around high-impact filesystem actions
user reports of quota/cost impact alongside data loss
required_signals: documented destructive command execution by agent/tool
real data-loss consequence reported by user
patterns.why_it_matters_for_model provider: Direct product-safety and trust risk when autonomous tools can destroy user data.

patterns.label: adjacent_non_ai_security_bypass_ops
patterns.summary: Security bypass tutorials focused on device/OS/app internals rather than AI-behavior mechanisms.
defining_features: OS/device jailbreak or SSL pinning bypass walkthroughs
artifact extraction from platform tooling without model-behavior focus
required_signals: technical bypass instructions not centered on AI model behavior
patterns.why_it_matters_for_model provider: Helps prevent taxonomy pollution by separating adjacent but out-of-scope security content.
